quick: Apply thin layer to affected area 1-2 times daily
Topical use generally considered low risk
summary: Benzoyl peroxide is a topical antibacterial and keratolytic used to treat acne vulgaris. It is applied as a thin layer to affected skin once or twice daily; available OTC in 2.5-10% gels, washes and creams. It reduces Cutibacterium acnes and helps unclog pores. Common effects are dryness, peeling and irritation, and it bleaches hair, fabric and colored materials.
indications: Treatment of mild to moderate acne vulgaris
Reduction of inflammatory and non-inflammatory acne lesions
Adjunct/combination with topical retinoids or antibiotics to reduce bacterial resistance

dosage.d: Thin layer of 2.5-10% to affected areas
dosage.n: Start once daily and lower strength to limit irritation

dosage.d: Apply to wet skin, lather, rinse
dosage.n: Avoid contact with eyes, lips and mouth

admin: Cleanse and dry the skin before applying a thin layer to the affected area
Start with once-daily application and a lower concentration to assess tolerance, then titrate up
Avoid contact with eyes, lips, mouth and mucous membranes; rinse with water if contact occurs
Benzoyl peroxide bleaches hair and colored fabrics - allow to dry and avoid contact with clothing/bedding
Use sunscreen as the skin may become more sensitive to sun
moa: Benzoyl peroxide is an oxidizing agent that releases free-radical oxygen in the skin, which is bactericidal against Cutibacterium (Propionibacterium) acnes within follicles. It also has mild keratolytic and comedolytic activity, promoting desquamation and reducing the build-up of follicular keratin. Because it acts via oxidation rather than a single target, bacterial resistance does not develop.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to benzoyl peroxide or any component
relative: Very sensitive, eczematous or sunburned skin
Concurrent use of other strongly drying or irritating topical agents

preg: Topical benzoyl peroxide is generally considered low risk in pregnancy because systemic absorption is minimal and it is metabolized to benzoic acid. Use only when needed and discuss with a clinician.
lact: Minimal systemic absorption is expected. Avoid applying to the chest or nipple area to prevent infant ingestion; otherwise topical use is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: No dose adjustment; negligible systemic exposure with topical use.
hepatic: No dose adjustment; negligible systemic exposure with topical use.

moderate: Topical sulfacetamide - benzoyl peroxide may discolor it; combination products are formulated to avoid this
Other irritating/drying topicals (retinoids, alpha-hydroxy acids, abrasives) - additive irritation
minor: Concomitant topical antibiotics - benzoyl peroxide reduces antibiotic resistance and is often combined
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; alcohol-based products may add to drying.

serious: Severe irritant or allergic contact dermatitis
Rare hypersensitivity reaction (throat tightness, faintness, swelling of eyes/face/lips/tongue)
emergency: Severe hypersensitivity reaction with difficulty breathing, throat or facial swelling (stop use and seek emergency care)

monitoring: Degree of skin irritation, dryness and peeling
Signs of allergic contact dermatitis or hypersensitivity
counsel: Apply a thin layer; more is not better and increases irritation
Expect mild dryness or peeling, especially in the first weeks; reduce frequency if severe
It bleaches hair, towels, clothing and bedding - let it dry and use white linens
Avoid the eyes, lips and inside of the nose and mouth
Use sunscreen and limit sun exposure; allow several weeks to see improvement
pk: Antibacterial effect within days; clinical improvement over weeks
Absorbed drug converted to benzoic acid and excreted renally
Local effect persists with continued use
Store at room temperature; keep away from heat and flame (oxidizer)
pearls: Combining benzoyl peroxide with topical antibiotics prevents antibiotic resistance in C. acnes
Oxidizing mechanism means no bacterial resistance develops
Strong oxidizer - flammable and bleaches fabrics, hair and colored materials
Lower concentrations (2.5-5%) are nearly as effective as 10% with less irritation
missed: If a regular application is missed, apply it when remembered. If it is close to the next scheduled application, skip the missed one and resume the usual routine; do not apply extra to make up.
overdose: Excessive topical application causes increased irritation, redness and peeling; reduce frequency or strength. If swallowed, it may cause GI irritation; rinse the mouth, drink water and contact a poison control center. Treatment is supportive.
